title: SPEED-Bench: a unified and diverse benchmark for speculative decoding
gist: 880 prompts across 11 kinds of content measure how many draft tokens are accepted, and a separate split measures throughput at long inputs and high concurrency inside production engines. Its argument is that acceptance is a property of the workload, not of the drafter.
changes: A way to measure the decoding lever on your own mix of domains before building anything. It also quantifies a rig error: load tests on random tokens overstate throughput by about a quarter.
caveats: Published by a company that ships its own drafters. The blog gives figures, not tables, for speed-up against concurrency.

numbers.metric: Throughput overstated by random-token load tests

bears_on.note: Acceptance follows the content: code and maths speculate well, chat and roleplay do not.
A load test on random tokens is a quarter too optimistic.
